claims.claim: Each part of an adventure gets a one-to-two-sentence overview entry tied to a Story Objective.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: its own entry of one to two sentences describing the part

claims.feature: NPC block: 'What They Want' and 'NPC Snapshot'
claims.claim: NPCs get a physical/backstory paragraph, then two single-sentence inline entries: What They Want and an NPC Snapshot retitled to a two-word epithet.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Location text is organized under Area Information with inline subheads such as Dimensions and Terrain and Lighting.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Bold in running text is reserved for creatures and significant keyed objects such as traps and secret doors, used judiciously.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Adventure sidebars give background that helps run a location and, except Playing the Pillars, avoid directly applicable rules content.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Encounters can carry a Combat / Exploration / Social triad of suggestions.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2023 AL template carries a CONTENT WARNING line on the cover and a Sensitivity Lead in the credits.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The adventure format defers to Chicago 17th and Merriam-Webster's Collegiate 11th for grammar and punctuation.
claims.source: DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The Word template defines the Boxed Text style solely for text a DM reads to the players.
claims.source: 1 - D&D AL Template.dotx (Jeremy Crawford, 2019-10) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: text that a DM is meant to read to the players

claims.claim: Epigraphs are not enclosed in quotation marks unless quoting a book that had them.
claims.source: 1 - D&D AL Template.dotx (Jeremy Crawford, 2019-10) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: An epigraph shouldn’t be enclosed in quotation marks

claims.claim: A sidebar that must immediately follow a passage is not a sidebar; integrate it into body copy.
claims.source: 1 - D&D AL Template.dotx (Jeremy Crawford, 2019-10) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: WotC's content standards forbid profanity in D&D products absent special approval.
claims.source: DnD Standards (Wizards of the Coast, 2020) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: D&D is described as mostly G-rated, sliding toward PG for mature themes or graphic violence; PG-13 products (Rick & Morty) need approval.
claims.source: DnD Standards (Wizards of the Coast, 2020) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: D&D is, for the most part, a G-rated game.

claims.claim: Standards forbid attaching traits to all members of a people, culture, religion, or sexuality.
claims.source: DnD Standards (Wizards of the Coast, 2020) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: Don’t attach specific traits or attributes to all members

claims.claim: Villains may be sympathetic but their evil must be called out as wrong; evil heroes are avoided.
claims.source: DnD Standards (Wizards of the Coast, 2020) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: their evil should be called out as awful and wrong
